title: Ash and Ambition
author: Claude, for Justin (Star Wars fan story)
summary: You are a low-ranked student at the Sith academy on Korriban, in the last years of the Brotherhood of Darkness. A quiet miner called Bane has just arrived, and he is asking questions nobody else dares to.

characters.name: Tesh
characters.about: Top-ranked student. Cruel because it has always worked.

characters.name: Bane
characters.about: A former miner, new to the academy. Huge, patient, watching everything.

yard.title: The training yard
text: Dawn on Korriban is the color of old blood. Forty students drill between the broken statues of the academy yard, and you are ranked thirty-first.
Tesh, ranked first, knocks the training saber from your hand without looking at you, then steps on it.

text.speaker: tesh
text.line: Pick it up. On your knees. That is where the Force put you.

text: At the edge of the yard the new student, the big miner they call Bane, has stopped his own drill to watch. Not Tesh. You.
yard.prompt: Everyone is waiting to see what you do.

choices.text: Challenge Tesh to the dueling ring
Pick it up, say nothing, go to the archives
Walk away and see where the miner goes

ring.title: The dueling ring
text: The ring is a circle of black stone on the academy roof. Overseer Maleth takes her seat. Challenges are always permitted here. So are funerals.

text.speaker: maleth
text.line: Thirty-first against first. Brief, I expect. Begin.

text: Tesh comes in fast and high, the way he always does. You have watched him do it to others for two years.

choices.text: Let the hatred take you and hit him with everything
Give ground, stay cold, wait for his mistake

ring-rage.title: First blood
text: Two years of swallowed insults come up all at once. The dark side answers like a flood through a broken dam, and Tesh's guard simply stops mattering.
He is on the stone with your blade at his throat before the Overseer has finished leaning forward. The roof is silent.

text.speaker: maleth
text.line: Well. Thirty-first no longer. The ring does not require mercy, student. It does not forbid it either.

choices.text: Finish him. Let the academy learn your name
Let him live, and let him remember who allowed it

ring-patience.title: A narrow loss
text: You give ground and wait. His mistake comes, a half-step too wide, and you see it clearly. You are simply not fast enough to use it.
The blow that ends the duel cracks two ribs. Tesh bows to the Overseer and does not look at you again.
As they carry the sabers away, a deep voice says quietly behind you: "You saw the opening. Most of them never do." When you turn, the miner is already leaving.
ring-patience.prompt: You lost. You also learned something.

choices.text: Go to the archives and find out how the old Sith fought

archives.title: The archives
text: Nobody uses the archives. The instructors say the old scrolls are history, and history is for the Jedi.

Deep in the stacks you find a shelf where the dust has been disturbed, and one manuscript left open. It describes the ancient Sith: not a brotherhood of equals, but a single Dark Lord, with all the power of the order gathered in one pair of hands.
A line has been marked with a thumbnail: when many share the dark side, each holds only a scrap of it.
archives.prompt: This is heresy against the Brotherhood. What do you do with it?

choices.text: Take it to Overseer Maleth and name whoever was reading it
Hide it under your robe and read it tonight
Wait in the stacks to see who comes back for it

follow.title: The Valley of the Dark Lords
text: You find him where no student is meant to go: the tombs in the valley below the academy, stripped bare by a thousand years of grave robbers.
Bane is sitting on a fallen pillar in the dark, a stolen manuscript on his knee. He does not seem surprised to see you.

text.speaker: bane
text.line: They told us the tombs are empty. They're right. The power that was here is gone, shared out, like rations in a mine. Every Sith a lord, and every lord weak.

text.speaker: bane
text.line: You came all this way. Ask your question, or draw your blade.

choices.text: Draw your blade. One heretic is worth a promotion
Say nothing, back away, return to the dormitory

night.title: The dormitory
text: The dormitory is a converted crypt, forty stone shelves in the dark. You lie awake thinking about scraps of power, and who is holding yours.
A little before the second moon sets, bare feet cross the floor toward your shelf. A hooded student, a training blade with the safety filed off, held low.
At the academy this is not a crime. It is how the rankings change.
night.prompt: You have a heartbeat to decide.

choices.text: Strike first, and make sure they never get up
Throw the blanket, run, and keep running into the desert
Catch the wrist and whisper: "Who sent you? I'll pay double."

end-feared.title: A name they whisper
text: It is over quickly. By morning the whole academy knows, and nobody steps on your saber again.
Overseer Maleth moves you up the rankings without comment. The others give you a wide path in the corridors, and you tell yourself that fear and respect are the same thing.
Across the yard the miner watches you with something like disappointment. He has seen strong, angry people before. They were all digging in the same mine he was.

end-leash.title: The Overseer's favorite
text: It reaches Overseer Maleth, as everything does. She hears you out with her fingers steepled.

text.speaker: maleth
text.line: Loyal. Useful. I can work with useful. You will bring me every whisper in that dormitory, and in return nobody will come for you in the night.

text: You rise through the rankings on her word alone. You are safe, and well fed, and you have never been less free. The dark side was supposed to break chains.

end-shadow.title: The student's student
text: He studies you for a long moment, then moves over on the pillar and turns the manuscript so you can both read it.

text.speaker: bane
text.line: Then learn this first. There should be only two. One to hold the power, and one to want it. I don't know yet which of those you are.

text: You read until the lamp gutters. When you climb back to the academy at dawn, the forty students drilling in the yard look, for the first time, like a great many people sharing very little.

end-dust.title: One more grave
text: You are fast. He does not even stand up.
The Force closes around you like a cave-in, a pressure he learned somewhere far deeper and darker than any classroom, and your blade goes skittering away across the tomb floor.

text.speaker: bane
text.line: You fought for a ranking. That is all they ever taught you to want.

text: The valley has room for one more grave. The academy lists you as a deserter and does not look very hard.

end-exile.title: The open desert
text: You run until the academy is a black tooth on the horizon, and then you keep walking.
No ranking, no master, no brotherhood. Only the red desert, the tombs, and a quiet in your head you have not heard since you were a child.
Years from now, when word comes that the Brotherhood of Darkness is gone, every lord of it dead in a single night, you will be one of very few people alive who are not surprised.
